newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police name lawmaker in MP death probe.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police name lawmaker in MP death probe.

text.p: Sri Lankan police on Wednesday were seeking to question an opposition lawmaker and two others in connection with the assassination of a member of parliament from the ruling coalition.
Gunmen killed People's Alliance parliamentarian Nalanda Ellawala on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals from the opposition United National Party (UNP).
A police statement on the killing was issued after Sri Lanka's two main political parties appealed for calm on the last day of nominations for local elections next month.
Ellawala's assailants also killed the guard of another ruling party legislator and wounded five people in the incident at Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo.

A lawmaker from the UNP, Susantha Punchinilame, his bodyguard and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former UNP mayor of Ratnapura, south of Colombo, were wanted for questioning over Ellawala's killing, said a senior police officer in the area, who declined to be named.
The descriptions matched a police statement released earlier on Wednesday about the suspects being sought for what the police said was the assassination of Ellawala.
Police have not issued any arrest warrants.
UNP general-secretary Gamini Athukorala could not be reached for comment after police named those wanted for questioning.
Ratnapura police said none of the people being sought had appeared.
"They seem to have gone into hiding. We're looking for them," said an officer at the Ratnapura police station.
Police said a local night curfew was imposed again on Wednesday and the army deployed after sporadic rioting and arson. There were no arrests.
Witnesses said they saw mobs setting fire to shops of opposition UNP supporters but a senior police officer in the area denied reports of widespread violence.

Around the country, extra police were on duty in election offices as candidates and flag-waving supporters filed applications for the polls, the first electoral test for the ruling People's Alliance (PA) since it came to power in 1994.
The polls will be held in seven of the country's nine provinces. The government scrapped polls in the northern and eastern provinces because of guerrilla activity by Tamil separatists.

A total of 3,567 seats in assemblies in 12 cities, 31 towns and 195 villages will be contested along with the posts of mayor in Colombo and 11 other cities. The size of the assemblies ranges from nine seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
Election day is tentatively set for March 27, with a firm date to be announced on Thursday, officials said.
